teams.heading: Fiji face debutant fly-half Domingo Miotti as Quesada tips tight Udine test
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has handed a first cap to Domingo Miotti, the Montpellier fly-half eligible through his Italian grandfather, for today's Nations Championship test in Udine. A run of wing injuries pushed Ange Capuozzo out to the wing, with Tommaso Allan at full-back. Quesada called Fiji a quality side and expects a tight game. For head coach Jake White's Fiji, bottom of their pool without a point, defeat or a win without a bonus sets up an Italy rematch in the sixth-place final at Twickenham.

lead.why: Fiji's own XV already ran, so the freshest Fiji-relevant story is what Quesada has picked to face them and why.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje links clearer England purpose to four-win run before All Blacks
teams.body: "It feels a lot more cohesive," England captain Maro Itoje told BBC Rugby Union Weekly, saying the squad's understanding of its game plan has grown campaign by campaign. Four straight wins over Fiji, Argentina, Australia and Japan followed five successive Test defeats. Discipline tells the story: 14 yellow cards and a red in England's first eight Tests of 2026, then none in two November Tests. Head coach Steve Borthwick credits that turnaround to his senior players. New Zealand arrive on Saturday after their first defeat by Wales in 73 years.

lead.why: It is the freshest England-specific story from the captain, and team selection has already run.

teams.heading: Anthony Jelonch back at No. 8 for France after shoulder surgery
teams.body: Former France captain Anthony Jelonch starts at No. 8 against Argentina at the Stade de France, Planet Rugby reports. It is his first Test since he was injured against England in the Six Nations. He told Rugbyrama that a hamstring problem came first, followed by a shoulder operation that was delayed because a nerve had been affected. He spent the summer rehabilitating at the CERS in Capbreton, then made his club return against Exeter on 18 October. Esteban Capilla makes his first Test start at six in a reshuffled back row, with Charles Ollivon at seven.

lead.why: A former captain's return to the France XV is fresh team news, distinct from the Rassie row and the goal-kicking story already run.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell moves Dan Sheehan to No. 8 for Springboks test
teams.body: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell's one real surprise in the matchday 23 spares hooker Dan Sheehan the energy-sapping scrum work the Springboks relentlessly attacked in last year's 24-13 win in Dublin. Rónan Kelleher, rated the best scrummager of Ireland's hookers, packs down between Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong. Sheehan did well at No. 8 for Leinster against Munster last month, though The42 flags his inexperience at picking the ball from the base of the scrum. South Africa remain 10-point favourites at the Aviva Stadium.

teams.heading: Quesada hands Domingo Miotti debut and Ortombina lineout role against Fiji
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has made only two changes from the side beaten by Argentina for Saturday's Round 6 test against Fiji in Udine. Montpellier fly-half Domingo Miotti starts on debut in place of Paolo Garbisi. Alessandro Ortombina replaces Federico Ruzza, who drops to the bench. Quesada said Ortombina was picked to lead the lineout and bring physicality. Injuries to wings including Lynagh, Faissal, Pani and Trulla keep Ange Capuozzo on the wing, with Tommy Allan at full-back.

lead.why: Today's new item is Italy's own team selection, led by a debut at fly-half, and it has not led an edition yet.

teams.heading: Scotland U20 beat Ireland U20 31-29 after trailing early in Cork
teams.body: Fergus Pringle's Scotland U20 side recovered from a nervy start on Friday night at Virgin Media Park. Ireland U20 led 7-0 through full-back Fionn Rowsome, and the sides were level 19-19 at half-time before the visitors closed out the win. Rory Caldwell, James Dalrymple, Christian Lindsay and Rory McHaffie all scored tries, backed by Harry Clark's kicking. The Irish Times judged Scotland worthy winners, noting the side had six players back from the group that finished fifth at last summer's World Junior Championship.

lead.why: A fresh Scotland result with full reporting, while the senior captaincy item offers only a headline with no names to stand on.

teams.heading: Wales v Australia moved to ITV4 as France v Argentina gets ITV2
teams.body: Steve Tandy's side lose the main channel for Saturday's Nations Championship finale against Australia at the Principality Stadium, WalesOnline reports. With all six final-round matches on the same day and kicking off in simultaneous pairs, ITV has handed the concurrent France v Argentina game in Paris to ITV2 and parked Wales on ITV4. ITV1 sticks with The 1% Club and I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! instead. The match stays free-to-air on ITV4 and ITVX, with Welsh-language coverage on S4C, S4C Clic and BBC iPlayer.

lead.why: The only new, sourced event about the men's XV's Australia test, and it changes how fans will find the match tonight.

teams.heading: Contepomi accuses Montpellier of breaking Justo Piccardo deal before France test
teams.body: Centre Justo Piccardo is missing from the Pumas group for Saturday's test against France at the Stade de France, and Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi says it was forced on him. Contepomi said Piccardo had played 11 weeks in a row, with his GPS numbers dropping in the last match to suggest fatigue. He accused Montpellier director of rugby Bernard Laporte and manager Joan Caudullo of breaking their agreement, leaving Argentina to manage the centre's workload over the past fortnight — an episode, he said, that revealed who can be trusted.

lead.why: A fresh, on-record row from Argentina's head coach explaining a selection absence on the eve of the France test.

teams.heading: Cardiff braces for another huge crowd as Wallabies close Wales' home campaign
teams.body: Principality Stadium manager Mark Williams expects another huge crowd for Wales' last home match of the Nations Championship, and urged fans to get in early for the anthems. Cardiff is still buzzing from Wales' 35-28 win over New Zealand last weekend, a result Williams called unforgettable. Great Western Railway and Transport for Wales are adding extra trains, though no post-match services will run through to London Paddington. Head coach Les Kiss's Wallabies arrive off a 12-15 defeat by Scotland, with one win from five.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones hails Gregor Townsend's Scotland tenure before Japan's Murrayfield test
teams.body: Before Saturday's Nations Championship test at Murrayfield, Japan head coach Eddie Jones said Scotland should be grateful for Gregor Townsend, defending the Scotland head coach against critics who note no Six Nations title or Triple Crown in nearly a decade. Jones won one of five Six Nations meetings with Townsend as England coach. “Scotland has been knocking on the door of the top four for a while now and, for a small rugby country, that’s a great achievement,” he said. Japan arrive off a 78-15 defeat by England.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett set for 150th Test as All Blacks face England
teams.body: Planet Rugby reckons Beauden Barrett is "lucky to be involved" in his 150th Test after the 35-28 defeat by Wales in Cardiff, though it credits his form against the Wallabies and Scotland. All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie picks him in the back three with Josh Moorby and the returning Will Jordan. Damian McKenzie replaces Richie Mo'unga at fly-half, with Mo'unga staying in the 23, while Quinn Tupaea's injury shifts Anton Lienert-Brown from 12 to 13 for Saturday's Test against England.

teams.heading: Franco Mostert starts at lock as training niggle sidelines Ruan Nortjé
teams.body: SA Rugby said on Friday that lock Ruan Nortjé, named alongside Eben Etzebeth on Monday, had been monitored all week, and that banned Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus took a cautious approach to give the 28-year-old more time to recover before Saturday's test against Ireland. Utility forward Mostert, a replacement against France and Italy, will win his 88th cap in his first start of the tour. Fellow World Cup winner Lood de Jager keeps his place on the bench as back-up lock.

lead.why: A confirmed late injury change to the Springbok XV is fresh hard news, unlike the uncited Marx footage debate.
